A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe X-Dancer, with matching core methods, equations, and experiments. All pages are readable. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally includes supplementary Sections 6–9.

before.justification: v1 reports original motion-generation and video-synthesis experiments, component ablations, and choreography fine-tuning results in Section 4, Tables 1–3, and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and additionally reports AIST-trained results, video-reconstruction ablations, dataset analysis, and user preferences, including supplementary Table 5.

M1.justification: The compositional confidence-aware VQ-VAE, cross-conditional autoregressive transformer, and AdaIN motion decoder remain unchanged. The AIST-trained variant changes training data, while naming SD1.5 supplies implementation detail rather than establishing an architectural change.

E1.justification: v2 explicitly adds a self-driven video-reconstruction scenario using source poses and ground-truth pose guidance in Table 4. The existing AIST/in-house dance domains, realistic and stylized characters, and Subject Three customization remain; the revised corpus size does not itself expand coverage.

E2.justification: Hallo, Bailando, EDGE, and Our motion + PG remain the main comparators. Table 4 adds GT Pose + PG as a reference and explicitly compares Single-Part + MD at the video level. Newly cited external methods such as DabFusion are not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds an AIST-trained motion-transformer control, addressing v1's stated inability to train on the competitors' dataset; its diffusion model remains trained on in-house data. Table 4 introduces self-reconstruction evaluation with PSNR and LPIPS. The reported corpus also changes from 107,546 clips averaging 30 seconds to 76,818 averaging 15 seconds, without establishing whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Existing pose-tokenization, context, and scaling ablations are retained. v2 substantially extends the documented evidence with video-level tokenization/decoder ablations in Table 4 and Figure 4, dataset-composition analysis in Section 6, and concrete failure cases in Section 9 and Figure 6. Subject Three fine-tuning is relocated, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2's participant counts and preference percentages document its user study but do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing entries in Tables 1–3 retain their numerical values. v2 adds X-Dancer-AIST results, Table 4 video-reconstruction scores, dataset statistics, and Table 5 user preferences, including 84.80% overall preference for X-Dancer. Table 4 also reverses the head/hand assignments of the pose errors reported in v1's Section 4.3; this is a reporting difference, not evidence of changed performance.

T1.justification: The VQ-VAE objective and autoregressive factorization in Equations 1–2 are unchanged. Renaming the joint-count symbol from J to P is not substantive. Neither version adds formal propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: zero-shot music-driven image animation, expressive 2D whole-body motion, transformer–diffusion integration, scalability, and customization. The first-framework and state-of-the-art claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning mostly frontal/freestyle training data, face and hand artifacts, color instability, and scene/identity inconsistencies. It attributes persistent rendering errors chiefly to the diffusion model using the ground-truth-pose control. It also removes the DIV target-distribution caveat and strengthens the BAS interpretation beyond Table 1: X-Dancer-AIST ties EDGE on AIST and scores lower on the in-house evaluation.

D1.justification: v2 documents third-party dataset sourcing, filtering thresholds, Qwen2.5-VL characterization, the SD1.5 backbone, and orthographic projection/alignment for baselines. It supplies the previously referenced user study's 25-video, 15-participant, randomized questionnaire protocol. A project-page pointer is added, while v1's code/model release promise disappears; actual resource availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges DabFusion's music-conditioned image-to-video generation and adds citations supporting animation, dataset analysis, metrics, and proposed future remedies. The central positioning around scalable 2D motion remains largely unchanged. Duplicate preprint/publication entries do not constitute additional research contributions.

P1.justification: The main section order and much of the prose remain intact. v2 tightens several passages, organizes the ablation discussion under named topics, and moves choreography fine-tuning into supplementary Section 8. Supplementary Sections 6–9 organize the added documentation and analyses.

P2.justification: v2 replaces examples in Figures 1 and 3, expands Tables 1–2, and adds the ablation display in Table 4/Figure 4, the user-study Table 5, and failure Figure 6. v1's choreography Figure 4 is retained as supplementary Figure 5. These substantially expand and revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 improves validation and transparency through the AIST-trained control, explicit video ablations, documented user preferences, dataset filtering, and concrete limitations. These gains are tempered by inconsistent reporting: the revised 76,818-video corpus is not reconciled with the retained 100k scaling discussion, head/hand error labels are reversed, and BAS superiority exceeds the tabulated evidence. The paper is better supported overall, but these unresolved discrepancies limit the improvement.
